entries.title: Ehrgeiz

emulation.notes: Use DuckStation with an owned PlayStation copy for the complete port, including the added characters and modes.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PlayStation port with optional emulator-side improvements; arcade emulation preserves the original but not the complete roster/mode set.

primary.why: The PlayStation version is the most complete version because it adds PlayStation-exclusive Final Fantasy VII characters plus Quest Mode and minigames, while still preserving the arcade fighting game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original PlayStation disc on compatible hardware, or use DuckStation with an owned copy; the Japanese PSN release is another route where available.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System 12 arcade fighting release.
all_releases.reason: skip: historically original, but it lacks the PlayStation version's extra characters and modes.

all_releases.fidelity: PlayStation port with extra Final Fantasy VII characters, Quest Mode, and minigames.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete version because the port adds exclusive roster and mode content.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only digital reissue of the PlayStation version for PS3/PSP/Vita.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful official digital route in Japan, but not a distinct higher-fidelity or more complete version than the PlayStation port.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The arcade original is historically first, but the PlayStation version is chosen because it adds exclusive Final Fantasy VII characters, Quest Mode, and minigames.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced official remaster or remake was identified; the 2008 PSN release is a Japan-only digital reissue of the PlayStation version.
